moments.alt: Sideways aerial reconnaissance print of wooded ground: white leader lines point to labelled equipment, missile trailers and tent areas, beside a black band reading MRBM FIELD LAUNCH SITE, San Cristobal #1, 14 OCTOBER 1962.

moments.quote: We could blow up a US ship in Guantanamo Bay and blame Cuba.
moments.short: We could blow up a US ship in Guantanamo Bay and blame Cuba.

moments.alt: White House tape of the first missile meeting, 16 October 1962: Kennedy asks the photo interpreter how he knows the object is a medium-range ballistic missile, and Arthur Lundahl answers, 'The length, sir.'

moments.quote: The cigars were so heavily contaminated that merely putting one in the mouth would do the job; the intended victim would not actually have to smoke it.
moments.short: The cigars were so heavily contaminated that merely putting one in the mouth would do the job…

moments.quote: WE AND YOU AUGHT NOT NOW TO PULL ON THE ENDS OF THE ROPE IN WHICH YOU HAVE TIED THE KNOT OF WAR, BECAUSE THE MORE THE TWO OF US PULL, THE TIGHTER THAT KNOT WILL BE TIED.
moments.short: …WE AND YOU AUGHT NOT NOW TO PULL ON THE ENDS OF THE ROPE IN WHICH YOU HAVE TIED THE KNOT OF WAR…

moments.alt: Sideways low-altitude photo of a cleared site among palms: a long white missile shelter tent and rows of striped fuel tank trailers, with printed labels MISSILE SHELTER TENT and MISSILE ERECTOR.

moments.quote: CIA to submit plan by 15 February for inducing failures in food crops in Cuba. Capability for sabotage of rice, for instance, is available; timing is the problem.
moments.short: Capability for sabotage of rice, for instance, is available; timing is the problem.

moments.quote: The fundamental cause of the disaster was the Agency's failure to give the project, notwithstanding its importance and its immense potentiality for damage to the United States, the top-flight handling which it required -- appropriate organization, staffing throughout by highly qualified personnel, and full-time direction and control of the highest quality.
moments.short: The fundamental cause of the disaster was the Agency's failure to give the project…

moments.quote: "We are out of ammo and fighting on the beach. Please send help. We cannot hold."
moments.short: "We are out of ammo and fighting on the beach. Please send help. We cannot hold."

notes: ExComm tape: window 244-255. Checked by RMS and by a local Vosk ASR pass (free and grammar-constrained) on 250-262 s: tape resumes at 243.6 after a digital-silence excision, speech from 244.2; '(How) do you know this is a medium-range ballistic missile?' 251.1-254.0; 'The length, sir.' 254.0-254.8; pause to 255.1; 'The what?' 255.2-255.4. End moved from 256 to 255 so the clip ends on Lundahl's answer, not on Kennedy's 'The what?'. Not checked by ear. The 'Excision 1, 9 seconds, excised' announcement is at 235.5-238.8 s. Khrushchev letters: the knot passage is on PDF p.21, the Moscow embassy telegram 1101 (section four of four), typed all caps with the telegram's own misspelling 'AUGHT'; quote and short keep both as printed. The short is cut at the commas after 'MR. PRESIDENT,' and after 'WAR,' (clause ends), so it keeps 'THE KNOT OF WAR' but leaves out 'the more the two of us pull...', which stays in the quote. The State Department translation of the same letter (pp.39-46) was not checked. Khrushchev face is 0.705 of the page width (above the 0.45-0.60 spec; kept, since a 0.60 box would cut the moment's own lines) because the telegram lines run from 0.13 to 0.89 and the short's middle line spans 0.13-0.815. Bay of Pigs: the mined p.40 beach message is grief:true, so I added a non-grief 'new' moment on p.42 (Kirkpatrick's 'fundamental cause of the disaster' paragraph) as the file's first moment, and the face is on p.42, so the default card is not grief. p.42 short is cut at the comma before 'notwithstanding'. Bay of Pigs face is 0.632 and Mongoose 0.62 of the page width, to keep full typed lines. Castro quote is on p.29 (printed page 22); Northwoods p.11 (printed 8); Bay of Pigs p.40/42 (printed 32/34); Mongoose p.9 (printed 7). Mongoose new moment is Task 21; the passage sits inside a hand-drawn margin bracket with a handwritten 'CIA 1.3(a)(4)' review mark. Mongoose quote drops the leading label 'Task 21:'. Both photos are printed sideways (rotated 90 degrees on the page); squares are given in the stored orientation. U-2 square is 1160x1160 px of full.webp (1850x2400), placed so the whole rotated '14 OCTOBER 1962', 'San Cristobal #1', the 22-40N 83-17W coordinates and the trailer, equipment and tent labels fall inside the inscribed circle; at 120 px the date band is what reads. Low-level square is 900x900 px of full.webp (1764x2400), on the missile shelter tent, its label and the fuel tank trailers. No video files in this topic. Skeptic pass: Khrushchev line 1 box tightened to start at 'WE' (was over the comma after PRESIDENT), line 3 and lens boxes end after 'WAR' (were over the following comma).
